subject: aviation
intro: Aviation leads to the cockpit and everything that keeps aircraft flying on time — airline and commercial flying, air traffic control, cabin safety and the maintenance crews behind every airworthy airframe.

roles.title: Airline Pilots, Copilots, and Flight Engineers
roles.entry: Bachelor's degree, FAA ATP certificate, 1,500 flight hours
roles.what: Captain and fly scheduled airline aircraft: plan routes and fuel, run checklists and preflight inspection, command the flight deck through weather and emergencies, and keep the aircraft inside regulations and performance limits.
roles.where: The aerodynamics, weather go/no-go decisions, performance and weight-and-balance, FAR/AIM regulations and instrument-flying units are the certification syllabus this career is examined on.

roles.title: Commercial Pilots
roles.entry: Commercial pilot certificate with flight training
roles.what: Fly for pay outside the airlines: charter and cargo runs, aerial survey and firefighting, crop dusting and sightseeing — often into shorter strips and uncontrolled airspace with less support than airline routes.
roles.where: The navigation and flight-planning unit — pilotage, dead reckoning, VOR/GPS, cross-country planning and airspace classes — plus ADM and human factors, match the self-reliant flying this work demands.

roles.title: Air Traffic Controllers
roles.entry: Associate's degree or FAA Academy training
roles.what: Separate traffic in the air and on the ground: issue clearances and vectors, sequence arrivals and departures, hand off flights between towers, centres and approach control, and keep flow safe when weather and emergencies compress space.
roles.where: Unit 8's phraseology, working towers and centres, and emergencies-and-lost-procedures topics, plus the weather unit's Metars and TAFs, are the operational language of this job.

roles.title: Aircraft Mechanics and Service Technicians
roles.what: Keep aircraft airworthy: inspect airframes and engines against maintenance schedules, test and replace components, sign off repairs, and ground aircraft until defects found in preflight checks are fixed and documented.
roles.where: Unit 1's airframe, engine and propeller systems, flight instruments and preflight inspection, plus the performance unit, teach the systems knowledge inspectors and mechanics certify against.

roles.title: Flight Attendants
roles.what: Run the cabin: brief passengers on safety, check equipment before departure, serve food and drink in flight, manage medical incidents and turbulence, and lead evacuation and other emergency procedures.
roles.where: The human-factors unit's physiology — hypoxia, vision, vestibular illusions — and CRM crew discipline, plus ADM risk models, are the safety science behind cabin crew training.
